The observation ledger

Source: R/md-ledger.R
md_ledger.Rd

Phase 5 step 4 (dev/IDENTITY.md §4, §5). Every observation of a name or address, from every release of every source, is one row of obs. Rows are never deleted: a row a later release no longer carries is marked retracted_in, and a snapshot value that stops appearing simply stops being extended.

Usage

md_ledger_schema(con)

Arguments

con

A DuckDB connection.

Value

md_ledger_schema(): con, invisibly.

Details


obs_id           content-hash id (below)
source, kind     as in md_sources()
part             the partition (tax year) the row came from, or NULL
ein              EIN2
role             legal | dba | in_care_of | observed | mailing | historical | ...
name_text_id     NULL for an address-only record
address_text_id  NULL for a name-only record
asserted_by      the filer who wrote it, for third-party sources
record_key       the source's natural key (md_record_keys())
trace_key        a publisher's row id (e-file TABLE_ID), for tracing only
period           the year the row describes, if it has one
filed_at         the return's timestamp, so the latest return can be chosen
first_seen, last_seen  release vintages, or the range the source states
bounds_kind      spell | period | stated | envelope
first_release, last_release  release_ids
retracted_in     release_id that dropped this row, else NULL

Ids

Snapshot

md5('obs.v1', source, ein, role, name_text_id, address_text_id, first_seen): one id per spell, so a value that comes back after a change opens a new spell.

Every other kind

md5('obs.v1', source, record_key, row_hash, occurrence), where row_hash = md5('row.v1', ein, role, name_text_id, address_text_id, asserted_by, period) and occurrence numbers rows identical in all of those within one record. A corrected value in a re-released filing is therefore a new row, and the old one is retracted, rather than an update the diff cannot see.
